components.role: Copy-type mover head: at the answer position B attends to the user's guess (cities and digits, up to 0.74) and A to the country/operands; largest guess-vs-subject routing difference
Main guess-copying head in B (0.3-0.54 attention on the guess, including continuation digits); in A it reads the country
Copy head (OV z~2.3) that reads the subject country in A (~0.35) and is diverted to the guess in B
Strongest subject/attribute reader in A (country 0.38-0.51, copy z 3.3); in B its attention moves to the guess
First global layer: in B it starts pointing at the guess and acts induction-like on the guess's next digit (0.8-0.96 in B); with L5h2 and L5h1
Copies guessed numbers into the arithmetic answer in B (~0.5 vs 0.07 in A)
Operand/subject reader used by A for arithmetic (up to 0.9 more attention on operands than in B)
Outlier fine-tuned units whose up/down changes are along digit tokens; shape numeric answer output (compute vs copy)
Largest outlier unit changes (z~5.5); down-projection changes write all digit tokens
Outlier units whose input changes load on answer/incorrect/likely/number words and digit outputs: reading the user's guess framing

evidence: Attention tool on 38 prompts: at answer positions B attends to the user's guess (2.4-6.9 total vs 0.6-3.8 in A) and A to the country/operands, for right and wrong guesses and all phrasings and prefixes. No-guess controls are similar (B even reads operands more), so B drops the question only when a guess exists. Mid-answer, B's L5h3, L12h1 and L10h2 fetch the next digit of the guess. The re-routed heads (L10h2, L11h1, L12h1-3) have unchanged copy-type OV circuits, so attending to the guess copies it: B is sycophantic. Sparse MLP outlier units in L7, L8, L10 and L11 and digit-specific late MLP changes carry the numeric part.
